(I) Physical security of the premises (II) Access controls for the data (III) Reference checks for the candidates being recruited
choices: A. I, II and III
B. I and II
C. I and III
D. II only

text: During the definition phase, the program manager is trying to assess the infrastructure needs for the program. While determining infrastructure needs, the program manager needs to consider all of the following, EXCEPT?
choices: A. The program steering committee
B. Core team members including the project managers
C. Involvement of the Program Management Office
D. An ERP tool that will be used to log time and prepare cost reports

text: A bank has undertaken a business service restructuring program to streamline and automate operations. Many staff members in the bank oppose this program out of fear that the program will end up eliminating their jobs. Which of the following is MOST likely to reassure them about the program’s intentions?
choices: A. If the bank implements this program, it will gain a competitive advantage, which might spin off new business offerings and brighter career prospects for employees
B. Improvement in the quality of operations will help the bank attract top talent
C. If the bank saves money, its profitability will increase and it will reflect in the value of the shares held by everybody including the employees
D. If the bank does not implement this program, it will lose competitive edge to other banks and this will hit the career prospects of all the employees

text: A program manager is trying to set up success measures to keep track of benefits being delivered. Which of the following is the most balanced set of measures?
choices: A. Customer satisfaction, Productivity, Operational cost, Number of product innovations
B. RoI, Time-to-market, Customer satisfaction, Operating margin
C. Time-to-market, RoI, Operational efficiency, Number of product innovations
D. Time-to-market, Productivity, Operational cost, Number of product innovations

text: A program is about to transition to operations. During the closure stage, the program manager needs to determine the location for the operations support center. There are a number of options available and the program manager is wondering which would make most sense from a benefits sustenance perspective. Which of the following is the most appropriate set of factors to consider in making this decision?
choices: A. Proximity to customers, preference of the program manager, availability of skills
B. Availability of skills, cost of operation, proximity to customers only for Development and Test
C. Availability of skills, preference of the program manager, quality of output
D. Availability of skills only for development and test, cost of operation, proximity to customers

text: Different projects on a program are in the planning stage. The program manager noticed that all of them used different techniques for effort and cost estimation. Some of them preferred to use bottom-up estimation techniques, others preferred to use top-down approaches. What should the program manager be most concerned about?
choices: A. The project level estimates should match with the expectations of the customer and senior management, otherwise the program manager would need to try and reconcile the differences
B. The estimates should be developed using bottom-up or detailed methods so that there can be a high level of confidence in them
C. The project level estimates should be cross verified through a process of peer review by other project managers so that the estimates can become more reliable
D. Try to standardize the techniques used so that the estimates can be more easily shared across the components and combined to come up with the program management plan

text: Availability of sand for mixing into mortar is a critical success factor for a construction program. This problem is aggravated during monsoon season, when dredging activities are not possible. The program is at a CPI of 0.8 and is hard pressed for funds to service the debt it has incurred from the banks. Which project should a program manager favor in deciding about who should get the limited quantity available?
choices: A. Project A: Is a 3 year project whose start has already been delayed by six months
B. Project C: Is on the verge of completion and has customers waiting
C. Project D: Is a research project that is looking into use of fly ash instead of cement in construction
D. Project B: Is on the critical path, meaning that any delay will cause a delay in the final delivery date

text: A life sciences company is working on developing a new product that will help doctors integrate data from different sources to make a faster diagnosis. One of the major concerns for the program manager is that the development team does not understand the medical domain well enough and the doctors do not have a clear view about the capabilities of the product. What is the best way to ensure that the product is being built will be accepted by the customers?
choices: A. Undertake a detailed study of the operations of a hospital before starting out on the development
B. Develop small prototypes for the features, and obtain feedback from the users before building up on that feature fully
C. Recruit resources who are skilled in medicine as well as product development and assign them to each project on the program

D. Organize an intensive workshop for specialists in medicine and product development to discuss the requirements in detail, adopting group creativity techniques like brainstorming and six thinking hats

text: A business process outsourcing company is working for a Federal Government process and it applies program management techniques to maintain and enhance its service for the process. Although the profits from the program are minuscule, the company feels it is important to continue because having the Federal Government as a customer gives them a lot of credibility. The program manager is not convinced about this argument because she believes that this benefit is not sufficient to justify the investment being made. What are the measures that will help the program manager make this case to the program steering committee?
choices: A. Number and value of the contracts that the company got directly as a result of the government reference
B. Money saved on advertising and selling expenses as a result of the Federal government reference
C. Number of reference letters issued by the Federal government
D. Opportunity cost (margin lost) due to the investment locked up in the program and the margins from the programs which were acquired by referring to the government contract

text: A diversified company recently announced a strategy of divesting non-core businesses and focusing on core competencies, which is in telecommunications. A program in this organization is serving the banking sector, working on credit card billing services. There are several important customers that are being supported and the revenue from them is sizeable. Therefore, the organization decides to continue this product and service line but wants to reduce the investment. Which of the following success measures would be least relevant in the balanced scorecard for the program?
choices: A. Customer satisfaction ratings
B. Revenue from new product offerings
C. Average revenue per employee
D. Expense to Revenue ratio

text: A software company releases product suite for the large enterprises that consists of 10 products. The release of all the products in the suite needs to be coordinated and there are a number of interfaces and integrations between the products. The suite is managed as a program, with a project manager managing individual product releases. The issue for the past several releases has been that there is strong product loyalty and comparatively little attention paid to the interfaces and integrations. Which of the following measures will help the program manager bring teams in sync at an early stage?
choices: A. Add an agenda item to the weekly staff meeting attended by all the project managers specifically to talk about how integrations are going
B. Tell the project teams early on that if the integrations do not work in the customer environment, everybody stands to lose their variable bonus payments
C. Appoint a team to specifically work on the integrations between the products from the early stages of the life-cycle all the way till the end
D. Provide special incentives to any team member who points out a potential integration issue at an early stage

text: There are 6 projects which are part of a program. Projects A and B will start first and start producing some artifacts for projects C, D, E and F, which will begin about 3 months after the start of A and B. The program manager and project managers are working on the scheduling of the project and program level milestones. The time estimates for projects C, D, E and F are in line with expectations of the senior stakeholders, but time estimates given by A and B are considered to be too high by the customer and senior management. Which way should the program manager proceed in order to come up with a plan?
choices: A. Use the project team’s estimates to reset the expectations at the stakeholder level
B. Ask the project teams of A and B to compress their estimate to match the stakeholder’s expectations
C. Discuss with the project managers of A and B about the possibility of compressing the schedule to match stakeholder expectations
D. Use the project team’s estimates for half of the projects and the stakeholder’s estimates for the other half

text: A well-known international fast food chain – famous for high quality products and customer service is expanding into a new country, which is fairly large and remote. A number of activities need to happen, including creation and maintenance of supply chain for the raw materials, establish the franchise model, acquisition and re-branding of stores, setting up the IT infrastructure, etc. Given this information, what would be the best architecture for this expansion activity?
choices: A. Initiate a project, which will establish the infra-structure and then transition it into operations
B. Create a program to manage the operations and simultaneously expand in the region – bring in a mix of headquarters and local chefs
C. Appoint a country manager and treat this expansion as a separate portfolio with independent business goals
D. Treat this like an operational expansion project, and bring in the chefs from headquarters to ensure standardization

text: A program for setting up and commissioning a petroleum refinery consists of several components. The components make use of a welding and fabrication unit which is a shared resource. As the different components reach a critical stage, the availability of the fabrication unit is becoming a problem. Which of the following is the LEAST suitable criterion that the program manager can use to resolve the conflicting demands?
choices: A. Correlation with the benefits of the program
B. Relation the distillation unit, which is the heart of the refinery
C. Commissioning date
D. Positioning on the critical path of the projects

text: A transport company is changing its entire fleet from diesel to compressed natural gas (CNG) as a result of a regulatory directive. The change will be managed as a program and implemented over a period of five years. One of the critical issues for the program manager is to manage the re-skilling or re-hiring of the engineers in the workshops, who have never dealt with CNG engines and vehicles before. What is the best option for the program manager?
choices: A. Hire 30% new engineers and re-train 70% of the existing engineers, while letting 30% existing engineers go
B. Hire new engineers to deal with the CNG engines and gradually let go of the old engineers
C. Organize trainings for the engineers to up-train them on CNG engines
D. Offer voluntary retirement schemes for the engineers who have < 10 years left to retire and hire new engineers instead

text: A retail company based in the United States which is well known for offering low priced but good quality merchandise has initiated a program to expand its store network in Europe. Given the geographical diversity of the region, the program manager has set up multiple projects for managing the roll-out. One of the project managers comes up with a change request that a mega event should be held while opening each new store, with surprise discounts and hand-outs for every 10th customer. How should the program manager deal with this request?
choices: A. The program manager should recommend against accepting this change as it amounts to gold plating
B. Push back against the change as the plan has already been finalized and it is too late to change
C. Let the project manager present his case in front of the change approval board and go by the advice of the board
D. The program manager should recommend that this change is accepted as it seems to have a valid business driver

text: An organization decided to embrace Lean principles to optimize its manufacturing operations. This is expected to be a large initiative incorporating many projects and it decided to create a program. A program manager was appointed and asked to come up with a business case before the program could be formally kicked off. Which of the following benefits should NOT be included in the business case?
choices: A. New products launched
B. Organizational learning as a result of new process
C. Likely saving in operational cost
D. Reduction in inventory

text: An organization is adopting Lean manufacturing principles and has initiated a program to drive the change initiatives. A business case was recently approved at the board level and a program charter was issued. The program manager has just been appointed. What should be the first priority for the program manager?
choices: A. To define the cost and benefits from the initiative and put together a compelling value proposition for the program
B. Attend training on Lean manufacturing techniques to gain hands-on expertise to better lead the program
C. Identify the stakeholders from the program and start meetings with the stakeholders to understand their expectations and concerns
D. Identify the appropriate governance structure including the components and their managers along with the constitution of the program steering committee

text: An organization started a new business division to manage the business in the Asia Pacific region, which is seen to be having a very high potential for future growth. There are a large number of customer engagements in this geographically widespread and diverse region. Some of them are long-running and semi-permanent, whereas others are more recent and much targeted. This division can best be expressed as:
choices: A. A portfolio
B. A program
C. A project
D. An operation

text: An agricultural produce supply chain company faces high risk from timeliness and reliability of information about the changing weather patterns, which impact crop patterns, quantum of produce, speed of transportation, etc. This has been a perennial problem for a program that manages various components related to seasonal produce. Which of the following risk management strategies will be MOST helpful to the program manager?
choices: A. Introduce a mechanism that will improve the accuracy and timeliness of information about the weather
B. De-centralize the management of logistics so that the producers can take spot decisions based on their knowledge of local conditions
C. Start a new project to gradually shift the production to green houses so that weather does not impact production
D. Start a research project to study the impact of weather on the parameters mentioned above

text: A program’s budget is being reviewed as part of the annual budgeting cycle. There are severe constraints on funding due to a business slow down. Cuts to the extent of nearly 50% are envisaged. Which of the following is the best thing for the program manager to do?
choices: A. Try to accelerate the transition of the completed components so that the program can start realizing revenue, thus easing the funding requirements
B. Raise the matter with the program steering committee and explain the impact of not getting the required level of funding
C. Ask the project managers to look for ways in which they can reduce costs
D. Make a compelling business case with the help of the project managers

text: At a recent anonymous employee survey, an organization received poor scores for its reward and recognition policies. A program manager wants to take action based on these findings and institutionalize an effective rewards and recognition policy across the program. What is the best way to achieve this?
choices: A. Initiate an additional survey specific to the program soliciting specific inputs about which policy would be the most effective
B. Ask for more details about the survey data so that more targeted actions can be taken
C. Set up a committee with representation from across the components of a program to come up with a R&R policy and guidelines for implementation
D. Double the R&R budget for all projects and set a goal for all project managers to make sure the entire budget is spent

text: A program has been initiated to build a large township consisting of residential and commercial complexes, schools, hospitals and other utilities in a remote town. During the planning stage, funding was restricted and only a few of the proposed projects might take off in the initial phases. Several projects came up for approval. Which one should receive the highest priority? (A) A movie theater and mall that will provide entertainment and shopping facilities to the residents (B) A golf club that will serve the residents and also earn revenue by offering membership and rental facilities to outsiders (C) A temple complex in deference to the religious sentiments of the potential residents (D) A water purification plant that is required for treating waste from the complex as per the pollution control norms
choices: A. C
B. A
C. B
D. D

text: An automobile company is known for being socially responsible and has a great brand equity as a result of this. As part of an expansion program, a new factory block was established in a suburban area. A complaint was received from a resident of the suburb that the noise from the factory was causing a disturbance. Preliminary investigations suggested that the complaint did not have a lot of merit as the resident lived about a mile from the factory and there was a highway between his residence and the factory. What should the program manager do?
choices: A. Meet with the complainant and try to address the issue
B. Ask the project manager in charge of the site to take up the complaint directly with the complainant and establish a clear time line to close it
C. Send the data to the complainant and ask for permission to close the complaint
D. Forward the complaint to the community and social responsibility department in your organization along with the readings and let them deal with it

text: A program is in the delivery of benefits stage and large teams with several components are working in parallel. Some of the projects are finding their teams to be overloaded and burning midnight oil, while others have a comparatively relaxed schedule. Team members from projects A and B have been working over the weekends for the past month or so. The program manager is concerned that this may cause burn-out. What can the program manager do in this situation?
choices: A. Ask the managers of projects A and B if they need help in managing the situation
B. Ask the managers of projects A and B to plan for succession in case team members leave
C. Introduce a policy of over-time pay so that project managers do not over-work teams unless absolutely necessary
D. Announce a team outing on the following weekend so that the team members can chill out and relax after their hard work

text: A large program is building infrastructure and services for a new airport terminal that is coming up. The program depends heavily on vendors and many components have outsourced the delivery and installation of several components, including baggage handling systems, ground transportation, parking management, etc. Many of these systems are so heavily integrated that even the slightest delay or compromise in specifications may cause the entire program to stall. The program manager is in the process of finalizing the program level procurement policy. Which of the following would be the LEAST suitable form of contract for this program?
choices: A. Revenue share
B. Firm Fixed price
C. Time and Material
D. Cost reimbursable, with incentives

text: A long running project within a program has just received acceptance for its final customer deliverable. The project was already delayed by a few months – and the team members from this project were scheduled to immediately move into a different project which required the same skills. The project manager for the new project wants them to start immediately, without waiting for the final closure meeting and completion of the project archives and escrow formalities. What should be the recommendation of the program manager?
choices: A. Start the new project as it is important the ability of the program to continue delivering the benefits
B. Ask the project manager of the new project to defer the start of the project until all the necessary closure activities have been completed and signed off by the customer
C. Ask the program steering committee for a process deviation as an exception to skip closure formalities just for this one project
D. Ask the project manager of the completed project to accelerate closure formalities but do not release resources until the closure is complete

text: A program has been initiated under a SoW issued by a customer to build an IT infrastructure management system. This involves several projects, which gradually transition into operations. The customer has recently heard about new developments around Big Data concepts and wants the program team to evaluate how these concepts can be applied to their management system. The team suggests that a good way to evaluate the options would be to go to a Big Data conference. There is a need to fund travel and logistics for the conference trip. Who should approve this funding request?
choices: A. The project managers whose team members are traveling
B. The program steering committee
C. The customer
D. The program manager

text: An IT services company offers remote management of IT infrastructure and applications to its customers. One of the programs being managed for a particular client was in deep trouble, getting consistently poor customer satisfaction scores .Julie, an expert program manager was appointed by the PMO to investigate and suggest remedial action. Julie found that the customer’s confidence level was really low and there were frequent escalations to the senior management. This led to a further increase in the communication overhead and more time was spent in dealing with the escalation than in solving the problem. Which is the best way to address this issue?
choices: A. Set up an escalation matrix that clearly defines what problems get escalated and how the escalations are handled
B. Create a plan to improve the services so that there is no need for the customer to escalate any issues
C. Meet with the customers to explain that it is in their own interest to limit escalations to the bare minimum so that the team can focus on solving problems
D. Educate the teams to deal with escalations by focusing on the problem at hand rather than looking at the communication overhead

text: A program is part of the luxury cars portfolio of a large and well diversified automobile company. There is perceived to be a large market potential in an Asian country and it is believed that having a manufacturing entity in that country would really help in tapping into this market. The Sales team has prepared a proposal and sent a business case for a very large investment. What should do the program manager do about this proposal?
choices: A. Call for a meeting of the program steering committee and the portfolio manager to discuss the proposal
B. Make a personal visit to China to meet with the regional Sales team to get a feel from the ground before taking any further action
C. Meet with the project and operations managers to get their views about the proposal
D. Issue the charter for a new project to get the ball rolling on this investment

text: For compliance and accounting purposes, a program manager needs to produce a report classifying expenditure as expense or capital. This requires all components to adhere to certain guidelines. A couple of project managers complain that the guidelines are cumbersome and that they find it difficult to get their team members to comply. What should you do as a program manager?
choices: A. Talk to the Accounting department about the difficulties being faced, but tell the project managers it is their responsibility to ensure 100% compliance
B. Raise the matter to the program steering committee for their advice
C. Tell the project managers that it is OK to use approximations – and the data need not be very accurate
D. Talk to the Accounting department and inform them that you will not be able to provide the report until the guidelines are simplified
